title: Sidney Desvignes band
summary: Three months with Desvignes after the boat; the rhythm and sax sections; Russell's meeting with a train cook.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And, um, yeah. Then after my playing on there, uh, on the boat, I joined Sidney Desvines group for about three months. Were they working here in town?
I know he was on the boat sometime too.

He was on the boat in later years, but that, at that time, he wasn't on the boat then. Uh, he was playing locally, playing spots from different places. And, uh, I remained with him for about three months. That's the band Pops Foster and Walter Pichon, Louis Bauerrand, that was, and I, we made the rhythm section. And Eddie Cherie and, uh, Adolf Alexandria and Walter Pearson was the saxophone section.

Oh, yes. I know, I met a man on the train, Professor Lynette and I went out there two years ago, and on the way back, he was a cook on the Southern Pacific, if that's the same man. He'd once played with Celestan, he'd said, and he'd best recognize him just walking through the train. So, then he visited him. I met him, that's the first time. I never did the same since.
Yes, he's a light-fledged follower. Yes, he lives in California.
I guess there wasn't any relation to the other Pearson, Eddie Pearson, who played the trombone.
I think that they were related, they were cousins. Cousins, huh? Yes, I think that they were related.
I just asked him, we've got to talk to him in about a half a minute. Just as the train is going over to Huey Long Ridge, he'd happen to be coming in, getting ready to get off.
